correctness.rationale: PASS: Projection of the contained unit ball onto each orthogonal factor ensures inradius >=1. Basit–Langi fixed-inradius simplex face-content minimization (plus tangential d Vol=r*surface for top coefficient) reduces each face polynomial coefficient to that of the regular inradius-one simplex. Face-measure convolution then reduces to regular factors T_d. Their explicit Phi_{d-2}/Vol=binom(d,2)*sqrt((d-1)/(d+1)) gives the exact product identity Phi_{n-2}/(2^n binom(n,2))=(prod A_d)(1-Sigma delta_d/binom(n,2)). The split for factors d>=3 (A_d>sqrt2 and Sigma delta<=alpha binom(n,2)) or only d<=2 (A_2>=3sqrt3/4 and binom(n,2)>=3 t) proves strict >1 whenever a factor has dimension >=2. All-segment boxes have equality precisely at side length 2; n>=3 matters since every side contributes to ridges. Independent low-dimensional convolution checks are corroborative, not all-n proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The planar polygon + interval theorem covers only factors dimension one/two and imposing additional admissibility constraints, and the triangle-product result stays in dimension-two factors. The submitted all-positive-dimensional-simplices theorem adds factors of dimension >=3 with only inball containment; no found stronger theorem implies these cases.

originality.rationale: PASS (best-of-knowledge): Zwierzynski poses the stronger general polytope ridge inequality as a conjecture. Earlier Resultary theorems on polygons with intervals and triangles only settle d<=2 factor products, and Basit–Langi gives one-simplex extremal face measures, not the mixed-dimensional product ridge coefficient identity and all-dimension sharp bound. This case with higher-dimensional simplex factors is a new, natural noncentrally symmetric subclass as far as available full text shows.
